skill_traces.query:
Sam: Hey Evan! I’m really getting into this healthier lifestyle—just took my friends on an epic hiking trip last Friday!
Evan: Hey Sam! That’s fantastic—nothing like a good hike to feel alive. We took the Prius for a long drive to the mountains last weekend. It was perfect until we got into a little scrape on the way back.
Sam: Oh no, were you guys okay after the accident?
Evan: Yeah, we were fine, thanks. Just a minor accident, but it put a bit of a damper on telling my work friends about getting married. They’ve been a great support, though.
Sam: I bet they were thrilled to hear about your marriage, despite the mishap!
Evan: Absolutely, it's been a whirlwind of emotions. Good thing the accident was minor. Just a reminder to take it easy on the road, I guess.
Sam: True, it’s important to stay safe. Glad you can still enjoy the peaceful moments after something like that.
Evan: Definitely, nature brings peace and clarity - it's a great experience.
Sam: Nature can make everything else seem small and help us find peace inside. It reminds us of the bigger picture, you know?
Evan: For sure, and nature has been a great healer. Speaking of which, I’ve got to share some of these new healthy snacks I’ve been trying.
Sam: They look healthy and delicious! Perfect for after a hike or, I guess, post-accident recovery, huh?
Evan: Exactly! They’re packed with nutrients and really easy to make. You also need to try these cookies, they are awesome! I’ll send you the recipes.
Sam: Thanks, I’d appreciate that. It’s good to find new ways to stay healthy. Do you have any healthier snack ideas?
Evan: Yeah, I've been trying to eat healthier too. Check out this cool recipe I discovered for these energy balls.
Sam: Do you like them? I know they can be an acquired taste.
Evan: I enjoy the taste of these. They're energizing and a healthy way to satisfy your sweet tooth.
Sam: Awesome! Always on the lookout for healthy snacks, thanks for the tip!
Evan: Glad to help - hope you enjoy it!
Sam: Thanks, Evan! I'll give these a try. They look yum. Your help means a lot to me. Btw you know what? I went to the store again and, unsurprisingly, had issues with the self-checkout. It's becoming a regular annoyance.
Evan: That's very strange, I've never had a problem with it once!
Sam: Apparently I attract that to me, if you ever want to be in that situation, call me at the store with you!

selected.name: Extract Each Self-Reported Event Separately
selected.description: Use when a message contains a speaker's explicit first-person past action with a relative time phrase.
content: Treat each explicit first-person past action in a message as a separate event candidate for that speaker.
Resolve the relative time phrase against the message/session timestamp to set world_start.
Do not fold the speaker's action into a candidate about another person or broader theme.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains explicit first-person past actions with relative time phrases, such as 'last Friday,' 'last weekend,' and 'post-accident recovery,' which qualify for extraction as separate event memories.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Concrete Events over Interpretive Summaries
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states a concrete event with specific participants and timing inside a broader narrative.
content: When a message states a concrete event such as receiving/giving an object at a specific age or time, create a separate event memory recording the giver, recipient, object, and timing.
If the same sentence also contains a broader statement, keep that derived state only as an additional memory; never let it replace the concrete event fact.
Ensure every concrete noun phrase appears in the memory content.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Event from Action Narrative
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user message explicitly describes a past incident and lists the concrete actions they took in response.
content: If a user message explicitly states a specific past event and lists concrete actions taken, extract one compact event memory capturing the event and the action sequence.
Keep all listed actions in a single memory rather than creating separate memories.
Only extract when the event is specific and the actions are explicit.
